title: Give human contributors a practical development walkthrough
lead: Turn the contributor pointer into a practical route through this repository, with a visual map of the implementation and links to the authoritative rules.
findings_note: Owner documentation review 2026-10-16; CONTRIBUTING.md:6 only points to AGENTS.md and ARCHITECTURE.md; ARCHITECTURE.md:19 describes layers as a plain text list. Existing project guidance already defines worktrees, tests, tracking and handoff, but lacks a short human-oriented walkthrough connecting these steps.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** changing architecture or project rules, a new contribution framework, duplicating the complete AGENTS.md instructions, new dependencies, or changing the landing procedure.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: A human contributor should know how to locate the relevant code, isolate a slice, validate it, and prepare a handoff without assembling the process from an agent instruction file and a detailed architecture reference.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- Expand CONTRIBUTING.md and add a Mermaid architecture diagram in ARCHITECTURE.md beside the current Shape explanation.
- Link to AGENTS.md, docs/how-it-works.md, and docs/landing.md for authoritative detail.
- Adjust README.md's contributor links only if required for discoverability.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: No automated prose test is required. Validate the development commands and diagram against existing project guidance and source. Preserve existing architecture documentation tests, including the git allowlist description, if surrounding text moves.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Walk through choosing a specified slice, reading its relevant code and acceptance criteria, creating its worktree before claiming it, implementing and updating docs, running appropriate checks, recording evidence, and handing off. Explain why affected tests accelerate iteration, why the full suite is required before completion when applicable, why slicer check is separate from code tests, and why git diff --check matters.

Use the repository's handoff policy and launch-directory commands targeting .worktrees/<id> with explicit PYTHONPATH and --root or git -C; do not require changing the session's working directory. Explain the docs-only test exception. Link to AGENTS.md for exact current rules, house style, setup, temporary fixtures, report requirements, and commands rather than maintaining a second full rulebook. Link to docs/landing.md for owner-authorized integration instead of repeating or performing it.

Add a Mermaid architecture diagram showing CLI and TUI calling shared operations, storage/JSON I/O, generated rendering, and check/verification. Verify arrows against the actual modules, preserve the single mutation path through ops, and keep non-ops rendering/sync/verification responsibilities clear. Explain the diagram in text and link to the conceptual guide for non-contributor terminology.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- A contributor can locate the subsystem relevant to a slice, identify the required checks, and prepare a reviewable handoff by following the guide's links.
- Review example command syntax and worktree paths against AGENTS.md; do not claim or implement another slice to test the guide.
- Review architecture arrows against source and existing invariants; verify changed links and anchors.
- Render CONTRIBUTING.md and the changed ARCHITECTURE.md with quire --config squalor to ignored .venv/docs-preview/ and inspect the diagram, labels, clipping, and pagination. Record any rendering blocker.
- Run affected tests, slicer check, and git diff --check. Follow the full-suite requirement if source or tests change.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Implement in a fresh slice worktree. Review documentation, tracking, and generated output together and finish with the required note and handoff after acceptance passes. Commit only when authorized. Merging, pushing, publication, and cleanup follow the owner's instructions.
